guards.what: N1: `CanEnchant` filters the candidate list BEFORE the shuffle and the offer (RoyalStamp.cs:35)
guards.rationale: Recorded because the order is load-bearing for G2's fix: the shuffle is applied to the FILTERED list, so the number of items the Rng orders depends on the deck's composition, and a fix that shuffles the whole deck and then filters would draw a different amount and diverge on parity. The sim's sibling relic/beautiful_bracelet builds its candidate list the same way round (filter, then select). Also note the contrast with batch 1's relic/beautiful_bracelet G1, which flagged the candidate-list filter as an open question needing Swift.cs -- here the filter's position is legible from RoyalStamp.cs alone. NOTE per binding rule 7: RoyallyApproved.cs, EnchantmentModel.cs and CardSelectCmd.cs are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: `.FirstOrDefault()` and the `cardModel != null` check (RoyalStamp.cs:36-37) -- an empty-deck / no-eligible-card path
guards.rationale: C# tolerates a deck with no RoyallyApproved-eligible card: the selection returns nothing, the null check skips the enchant, and the relic simply does nothing -- but the UnstableShuffle has still run, so G2's stream draw happens even in that case (a shuffle of an empty or single-element list still consumes what UnstableShuffle consumes for that length). Recorded so a fix does not put the shuffle inside an `if candidates` guard and silently diverge on decks with no eligible card. Recorded as faithful because the port's do-nothing behaviour happens to match this arm exactly; every other arm is G1's.
